Header:

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan with Redwood Inference, this is Priya our solutions engineer, quick round of intros?
[00:12] Daniel Park: yeah Daniel Park, CISO at Novus. thanks for setting this up. we sent over a SIG and a couple custom security questions, hoping to walk through line items and evidence expectations.
[00:24] Priya Sharma: great, thanks Daniel. real quick agenda: SOC 2 / ISO posture, SSO/RBAC, audit logging, encryption/KMS, data residency, and then we can go through the SIG spreadsheet row by row for anything unclear. sound good?
[00:36] Marta Gomez: sounds good. also want to flag that our legal team may follow up on data processing agreements and subprocessor lists.
[00:44] Evan Li: and procurement will need contractual SLAs and a red-team report if available.
[00:50] Jordan Lee: totally, we can cover where those live; SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs are stored on our compliance portal, i'll share links after. we also have a regularly updated subprocessor list.
[01:05] Daniel Park: can you confirm scope of SOC 2 - is it production and supporting services? sometimes vendors exclude infra components and that causes trouble.
[01:15] Jordan Lee: yes, our SOC 2 covers production inference and the control plane services used for monitoring and billing - um, there was a line about third party infra, I can clarify in the report. (pause) Also note we have SOC 2 from a Big4 auditor, and ISO 27001 in scope for the control plane.
[01:36] Marta Gomez: ok, please include auditor contact info when you share.
[01:40] Priya Sharma: noted. on SSO, we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, role-based access control - you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles. small caveat: custom roles for advanced permissions are planned in the roadmap, today we have admin/editor/viewer and service roles.
[02:02] Daniel Park: what about RBAC for dedicated/private deployments vs hosted? we need to ensure separation between sandbox and prod.
[02:12] Priya Sharma: good question - for Dedicated and Private we expose tenancy-level RBAC you can tie to your IdP and enforce separate tenants for sandbox/prod, and we have route-level permissions for model deployments. sometimes the transcript AI writes 'route' as 'root', sorry.
[02:32] Sana Reddy: do you support SCIM for auto-provisioning from our Okta?
[02:36] Priya Sharma: yes, Okta and Azure AD are supported via SCIM; provisioning runs over a secure API, and we log provisioning events to the audit log.
[02:46] Daniel Park: audit logs - retention and export? we typically require 12 months immutable logs, with S3 export and support for SIEM ingestion.
[02:56] Jordan Lee: we retain high-fidelity audit logs for 13 months by default for enterprise plans, exports to customer S3 or secure syslog are supported, and we can ship to Splunk / Datadog via secure connectors. for regulatory needs we can extend retention and provide tamper-evident storage options.
[03:16] Marta Gomez: tamper-evident, can you describe?
[03:18] Priya Sharma: sure - we use write-once storage for audit records and checksum verification, and store checksums in an append-only ledger; in private deployments you can manage the ledger yourself if you want. (some overlap)
[03:34] Daniel Park: encryption - at rest and in transit? key ownership?
[03:38] Jordan Lee: all customer data in transit is TLS 1.2+, we prefer 1.3; at rest we encrypt with AES-256. For key management you can choose Redwood-managed KMS or bring-your-own KMS (BYOK) via customer KMS/HSM providers - we integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and external HSMs.
[04:00] Marta Gomez: BYOK - does Redwood have access to keys in any mode?
[04:04] Priya Sharma: with BYOK, keys are provisioned and controlled by the customer; Redwood never stores plaintext keys. We may have encrypted key handles for automated operations but cannot decrypt without customer KMS permissions. For on-prem/private we can integrate with local HSMs.
[04:22] Daniel Park: key rotation policy?
[04:24] Jordan Lee: we recommend 90-day rotation for application keys, customer-controlled master keys can be rotated as you dictate; we support automated rewrap operations. we'll share key rotation SLA and automation scripts.
[04:36] Evan Li: evidence - what files can you provide for SIG? e.g., KMS config screenshots, access control lists, encryption process docs, config management evidence.
[04:46] Priya Sharma: yes, we can provide config exports, runbooks, screenshots, logs showing key operations, and auditor attestations. some artifacts are redacted in hosted environments for multi-tenant info but we provide per-customer evidence for Dedicated/Private.
[05:02] Daniel Park: data residency - we need EU-only storage for a subset of PII. is that possible?
[05:08] Jordan Lee: yes, we support region pinning for data-at-rest for dedicated and hosted enterprise customers; for hosted we have EU regions and we can configure tenant-specific regional controls. for strict EU-only we may recommend Dedicated or Private depending on throughput needs.
[05:24] Marta Gomez: can you confirm backups and DR location? backups must remain in the region.
[05:30] Priya Sharma: backups can be region-restricted for EU-tenants, and DR can be configured to replicate to an approved secondary region - we document RTO/RPO in the runbook.
[05:46] Daniel Park: on the SIG spreadsheet there were a bunch of CAIQ questions about network segmentation and egress filtering, shall we go row by row?
[05:56] Jordan Lee: sure, let's open the spreadsheet - (screen share note: Jordan toggles spreadsheet)
[06:08] [06:08] Jordan Lee: Row 3, question about network segmentation: Redwood uses VPC isolation for customer workloads, security groups limit egress, and egress to customer-owned endpoints is allowed via private link; for hosted customers we use tenancy isolation and per-tenant vnet peering where applicable.
[06:30] Marta Gomez: what about outbound model calls to third party APIs, like integrations? we need control and approval process.
[06:38] Priya Sharma: outbound integrations are configurable per-tenant, and you can whitelist domains and disable external calls; we log all outbound calls in audit logs.
[06:50] Daniel Park: incident response - playbook and SLA for notification?
[06:54] Jordan Lee: we have an IR playbook, 24/7 SOC for enterprise customers, and incident classification with 1 hour initial notification for sev1. we'll share the runbook excerpt.
[07:08] Marta Gomez: do you run regular pentests and red team?
[07:12] Priya Sharma: yes, annual external pentests, quarterly vulnerability scans, and some targeted red-team exercises annually. we can provide summary reports and remediation timelines.
[07:24] Evan Li: any certifications for crypto modules or HSM?
[07:28] Jordan Lee: we integrate with FIPS-compliant HSMs and can provide details; HSM vendor certs are available.
[07:36] Daniel Park: ok on evidence items we need: SOC 2 report, ISO cert, auditor contacts, KMS diagrams, key rotation policy, audit log retention confirmation, backup/DR region info, pentest summary, subprocessor list, and DPA template.
[07:52] Jordan Lee: got it - i'll compile and share via secure share link.
[07:56] Marta Gomez: one more: do you support customer-controlled logging endpoints? we want logs to go to our Splunk instance.
[08:02] Priya Sharma: yes, we can stream logs to customer SIEM (S3, syslog, or direct Splunk HTTP event collector) and can configure mutual TLS for the stream.
[08:14] Daniel Park: any limitations on log volumes and costs?
[08:18] Jordan Lee: we'll include recommended retention and cost estimates; high-volume logs can be compressed and tiered.
[08:26] [small crosstalk]
[08:32] Daniel Park: procurement question, what about indemnity and security-related SLA credits?
[08:36] Jordan Lee: our enterprise contract includes security-related SLAs and data breach indemnities; we can share standard contract language and negotiate in legal review.
[08:46] Marta Gomez: on the SIG question about change management evidence - do you keep change tickets and approvals?
[08:51] Priya Sharma: yes, we keep audit trails in our ticketing system with approvers and change windows; we can export redacted tickets as evidence.
[08:58] Daniel Park: great. can we get an inventory of subprocessors?
[09:02] Jordan Lee: yes, we'll share the most recent subprocessor list and dates of assessment.
[09:08] Evan Li: timeline - after we get the docs we'll run through legal and security; target is vendor decision by end of October.
[09:16] Jordan Lee: sounds good - next steps we'll bundle docs and share the SIG answers; if you want we'll do a second technical deep-dive on KMS/HSM and runbook integration.
[09:28] Marta Gomez: yes please, technical runbook review would be helpful.
[09:32] Priya Sharma: i'll prepare a 45-minute deep-dive and include sample automation for key rotation and log exports.
[09:40] Daniel Park: quick question - do you have a model for minimizing customer data in logs, like PII scrubbing?
[09:46] Priya Sharma: yes, we support configurable redaction and PII scrubbing at ingest, with community detection and custom regex rules, and we recommend pre-processing for ultra-sensitive data.
[09:58] Jordan Lee: ok, looks like we have action items; i'll recap.
[10:02] Jordan Lee: Recap: Jordan to send SOC 2, ISO cert, subprocessor list, and completed SIG answers; Priya to send KMS diagrams and schedule the technical runbook session; Novus to confirm residency requirements and prioritized SIG questions.
[10:18] Evan Li: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[10:22] Jordan Lee: thanks all, end call.
